title: Shishunala Sharifa — The Saint Poet of Karnataka

scenes.title: Shishunala Sharifa
scenes.body: Saint-poet, social reformer, and the first Muslim poet of Kannada literature
scenes.narration: Shishunala Sharifa. Born 1819, died 1889. He was a saint poet, a social reformer, and the first Muslim poet in Kannada literature. His life and work transcended religious boundaries.
scenes.gen_prompt: A mystical 19th century portrait of a bearded Sufi saint in traditional attire, warm golden sunset lighting, spiritual atmosphere, ambient glow, historical Indian aesthetic

scenes.title: The Unifier
scenes.subtitle: Sufi meets Bhakti
scenes.body: Fused Islamic Sufi mysticism with Hindu Bhakti tradition in his poetry
scenes.narration: Sharifa was a rare unifier. He fused Islamic Sufi mysticism with the Hindu Bhakti tradition. His poetry spoke one language — the language of the heart.
scenes.gen_prompt: An old Indian temple and a mosque side by side, golden hour light, spiritual harmony, architectural fusion, warm earthy tones, peaceful atmosphere

scenes.title: Tatvapadagalu
scenes.subtitle: Philosophical Poems
scenes.body: Simple Kannada verses carrying profound spiritual truths about life, mind, and the divine
scenes.narration: His Tatvapadagalu are philosophical poems. Simple Kannada verses that carry profound spiritual truths. Each poem is a mirror held up to the human condition.
scenes.gen_prompt: Ancient Kannada palm leaf manuscripts with poetic script, warm candlelight illumination, rustic Indian setting, spiritual scholarly atmosphere, deep amber tones

scenes.title: The Wild Horse
scenes.subtitle: Mind as Battlefield
scenes.body: His most famous metaphor — the restless mind is a wild horse that must be tamed through self-awareness
scenes.narration: His most famous metaphor: the mind is a wild horse. It gallops unrestrained through desires and fears. His poetry teaches us to tame this horse through self-awareness.
scenes.gen_prompt: A majestic wild horse galloping freely across an open field at sunset, dramatic sky, motion blur, spiritual symbolism, wide landscape, golden and amber tones

scenes.title: Beyond Labels
scenes.subtitle: Formless Divine
scenes.body: Rejected caste, creed, and ritual — taught devotion to a formless divine through ethical living
scenes.narration: Sharifa rejected caste, creed, and empty ritual. He taught devotion to a formless divine. Not through temples or mosques, but through ethical living and inner purity.
scenes.gen_prompt: A luminous abstract formless light radiating through clouds, spiritual transcendence, ethereal golden beams, people from diverse backgrounds looking upward, unity in diversity

scenes.title: Question Everything
scenes.subtitle: Social Critique
scenes.body: Used biting satire to expose hypocrisy in religious orthodoxy and superstition
scenes.narration: He used biting satire to expose hypocrisy. Religious orthodoxy, superstition, empty rituals — nothing escaped his sharp poetic critique. His words cut through pretense.
scenes.gen_prompt: A wise old figure speaking to a gathered crowd in a village square, dramatic storytelling scene, warm sunset lighting, rustic Indian village setting, thought-provoking atmosphere

scenes.title: For Spiritual Speakers
scenes.subtitle: Timeless Relevance
scenes.body: His poetry provides ready metaphors for modern spiritual discourse across all faiths
scenes.narration: For today's spiritual speaker, Sharifa is gold. His poems offer ready metaphors that work across any faith. The wild horse, the mirror, the lamp — these images speak directly.

scenes.title: The Lamp Within
scenes.subtitle: Universal Wisdom
scenes.body: His message: the divine is not outside you — it is the lamp already burning within
scenes.narration: His core message: the divine is not outside you. It never was. It is the lamp already burning within. His Tatvapadagalu simply help you turn your gaze inward.

scenes.title: Shishunala Sharifa
scenes.subtitle: Eternal Guide
scenes.body: His Tatvapadagalu continue to guide seekers across religions, cultures, and generations
scenes.narration: Shishunala Sharifa passed away in 1889. But his Tatvapadagalu live on. They continue to guide seekers across religions, cultures, and generations. A poet for all time.
